hypotheses_tested: H1 — the new host check is decorative: the UNC test would pass with or without it. REJECTED by mutation. Reverting externalUrls.ts:66 to the r2 pathname-only form turns exactly one test red (`blocks a UNC host serving the same pathname`); restoring makes 25/25 green again. The test genuinely pins the host dimension that r2 proved was previously untested.

H2 — some other file: host spelling still normalizes to the shipped document's empty host and fails open. REJECTED after probing 10 hostile file: URLs through Node's WHATWG parser against `file:///opt/sloodge/resources/renderer/index.html`. `file://EVIL.example/<same path>` -> host 'evil.example', blocked. `file://[::1]/...` -> host '[::1]', blocked. `file://127.0.0.1/...` -> host '127.0.0.1', blocked. `file://evil.example:445/...` throws (file URLs cannot carry a port), so `host` vs `hostname` cannot be played off each other — and `host` is the stricter choice regardless. `file:////evil.example/<same path>` and the backslash form `file://\\evil.example\...` both normalize to host '' but pathname `//evil.example/opt/...`, which differs from the app pathname, so they are blocked by the second conjunct. The only inputs that pass are `file://localhost/<same path>` and `file://LOCALHOST/<same path>`, which the parser normalizes to the empty host per the URL spec — these denote the identical on-disk file, so allowing them is correct, not a bypass. No fail-open found.

H3 — appUrl (derived from `import.meta.url`) and the document Electron actually loads (via `loadFile(fileURLToPath(...))`) can disagree on percent-encoding for awkward install paths, so a legitimate reload breaks or, worse, a foreign path matches. REJECTED. Round-tripped four hostile install paths through `pathToFileURL`: a space -> `%20`, `#` -> `%23`, a literal `%` -> `%25`, non-ASCII -> UTF-8 percent-encoding. Both sides derive from the same encoding rules and, critically, from the same `import.meta.url` object (index.ts:7-8 splits one URL into the href used for the policy and the path fed to loadFile), so drift is impossible by construction — and any hypothetical divergence fails closed (blocked reload), never open.

H4 — the scheme allow-list still lets something dangerous out via `mailto:`, whose href is forwarded verbatim. REJECTED as a defect. `mailto:a@b.co?subject=hi%0Abcc:c@d.co` survives parsing with `%0A` intact, and a literal newline is stripped by the parser rather than preserved, so no raw CR/LF reaches the OS. The residual capability — a prefilled bcc/attach parameter in the user's mail composer — is the ordinary web-platform behavior of any `<a href="mailto:">` in any browser, requires the user to press send, and is the deliberate, documented scope of the allow-list. Strictly narrower than the pre-fix behavior, which forwarded every scheme.

H5 — the fix is incomplete: another code path still reaches `shell.openExternal` or opens a window unguarded. REJECTED. Grepped `src/` for `openExternal|window.open|setWindowOpenHandler|will-navigate|will-redirect|will-frame-navigate|webRequest`: exactly one `shell.openExternal` call site (index.ts:37, behind `toSafeExternalUrl`), one `setWindowOpenHandler` (index.ts:34, returning `action: 'deny'` unconditionally), one `will-navigate` listener (index.ts:48). No second entry point, and the app menu does not open URLs.

H6 — a redirect or a subframe navigation slips past `will-navigate` (Electron 43 fires it for the main frame only; redirects surface as `will-redirect`). REJECTED as unreachable for this build, and deliberately not raised as a finding. A redirect can only follow a navigation the guard already allowed; in production the only allowed target is the local packaged index.html, which cannot redirect, and in dev the only allowed origin is the developer's own Vite server. Subframes: the app currently renders no iframes at all (app-shell milestone), and the planned slide iframes are opaque-origin `sandbox="allow-scripts"` frames that cannot top-navigate or reach the preload bridge, so a self-navigating slide frame gains nothing it did not already have via `fetch`. Worth a `will-frame-navigate` listener when slide iframes land; not a defect in this changeset.

H7 — the change violates a repo hard rule (dependency direction, sandbox weakening, new dependency). REJECTED. `src/main/security/externalUrls.ts` imports nothing at all — it is pure Node/WHATWG, which is what makes it Vitest-reachable per 70-testing-ci.md's pure-function rule; no `oxlint-disable` anywhere in the diff; `.oxlintrc.json`'s `no-restricted-imports` overrides are satisfied; `webPreferences` (sandbox/contextIsolation/nodeIntegration/webviewTag) is untouched by the diff; no package.json change. No `any`, `as`, `!`, or `@ts-expect-error` in the new code — the trust-boundary input (a renderer-influenced URL string) is validated by parsing plus an allow-list, not asserted.

As in r1 and r2, this environment cannot launch Electron, so the will-navigate and setWindowOpenHandler wiring is reasoned from Chromium navigation-throttle semantics and Electron docs rather than observed. The policy module itself — where all the decisions live — is fully exercised by Vitest.

notes.summary: Confirmation round: both r2 findings are genuinely fixed and the fix is revert-proof. The file: branch now requires host equality as well as pathname, with a comment naming the Windows UNC/SMB hazard, and the new test at external-urls.test.ts:84 is the one that reds when I revert the host conjunct — closing exactly the untested dimension r2 identified by applying-and-reverting the same one-liner. The dead `origin !== 'null'` clause is gone without loss of coverage. Fresh-eyes pass over the final module found no new defect: ten hostile file: host spellings all fail closed (only the spec-mandated `file://localhost` normalization passes, and it denotes the same file), install-path encoding cannot drift because both sides come from one URL object, `mailto:` forwards nothing a browser would not, and there is exactly one openExternal call site in the tree. Self-run green across oxlint, prettier, typecheck, and 209 tests. Zero blockers, zero majors, zero minors — ship it.
